gist: US death row inmate Christa Pike is unconscious after a failed lethal injection execution.
Lawyers claim prison officials botched the execution by failing to insert IV lines correctly.
Tennessee's governor ordered an independent review and halted all executions for the year.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: US death row inmate Christa Pike is unconscious and on a ventilator following a failed execution attempt. Her lawyers filed an emergency motion to preserve evidence, alleging prison officials botched the lethal injection. They state officials used at least seven needles, bending one, while Pike whimpered and cried. An expert suggested the drug pentobarbital entered tissue under her skin rather than her bloodstream due to ruptured veins or blood clots.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has halted all executions in the state for the year and ordered an independent review. Pike's lawyers had previously warned that her blood-clotting condition and small veins risked causing unnecessary pain.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Authorities have not yet said whether they will attempt to execute Pike again, and her lawyers are seeking to preserve all physical, written, and electronic evidence.

fivew: A failed execution attempt left a death row inmate unconscious and on a ventilator.

gist: Spanish pensioner Maricarmen Abascal has died following her eviction from her Madrid flat.
Her eviction ignited nationwide protests, encampments and widespread anger over Spain's housing crisis.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Eighty-seven-year-old Maricarmen Abascal died in hospital two weeks after being removed on a stretcher from her Madrid home of over seven decades. The flat's owner had significantly raised her rent, which exceeded her pension. Although the firm later offered a return agreement, Abascal died before signing. Her eviction sparked mass demonstrations across Spain.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Abascal became a national symbol of the housing crisis. Tens of thousands protested, setting up encampments in Madrid and other cities. The outrage triggered major political instability when parliament rejected emergency housing legislation. Consequently, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap general election for 29 November, seeking a broader progressive majority to overcome conservative resistance.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Unions have scheduled a general strike for 11 November. Parliament's permanent council will vote on two newly approved cabinet housing decrees containing 21 measures. Meanwhile, Spain heads to the polls on 29 November, with opinion polls suggesting the conservatives are likely to finish as the largest party.

gist: Pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton has died at the age of 90.
Hamilton led the software development for Nasa's Apollo missions, saving the 1969 moon landing.
She coined the term software engineering and received a presidential medal in 2016.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Computer pioneer Margaret Hamilton has died aged 90, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology announced. The Guardian reported she died on 30 September, while Ars Technica noted she died last week. Hamilton learned programming at MIT, worked on weather simulations and air defence projects, and became the first programmer and first woman hired by MIT's Instrumentation Lab for Nasa's Apollo programme. In 2016, President Barack Obama presented her with the nation's highest civilian honour, which the BBC called the Presidential Medal of Honor and other outlets identified as the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Hamilton coined the term software engineering and directed the Apollo onboard flight software development. During the 1969 Apollo 11 moon landing, her software's failsafe mechanisms compensated for computer overloads, averting an abort and allowing the Eagle module to land safely.

gist: Indonesian groups filed a lawsuit accusing the government of gross negligence over wildfires.
The toxic haze has closed schools and caused respiratory illnesses across South-east Asia.
Government defendants failed to attend the opening court hearing, delaying proceedings until October.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Indigenous and civil society groups in Borneo filed a lawsuit against Indonesian officials, including President Prabowo Subianto, over toxic haze from wildfires. The defendants failed to attend the opening court hearing in Pontianak, causing an adjournment.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The annual fires, often lit to clear land for palm oil, have caused severe air pollution, closed schools, and triggered respiratory illnesses across South-east Asia. Plaintiffs accuse the government of ignoring warning signs and want the crisis classified as a national disaster.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The court hearing has been adjourned until 21 October. The lawsuit seeks comprehensive recovery measures, including covering residents' healthcare costs.

sections.text: The country's fragile healthcare system is struggling to cope with severe blood shortages and limited resources. Civilians bear the brunt of the violence, which intensified after President Salva Kiir suspended Vice-President Riek Machar following a rebel attack.

The event aims to boost the profile and visibility of women's sport.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: England has been chosen to host the 2031 Netball World Cup in Manchester. The matches will take place at the Co-op Live indoor arena. This decision was announced by World Netball and England Netball during the national governing body's centenary year. It will be the fourth time the country has hosted the tournament, which was last held in England in 2019 in Liverpool.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Organisers believe the tournament will help increase the visibility and impact of netball and women's sport across the UK. It also offers an opportunity to inspire future players and fans. England's team, the Roses, previously reached the final in 2023 and finished as runners-up in 1975, but they have yet to win the tournament.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Co-op Legal Services has introduced an OpenAI-trained system to record, analyse and score customer phone calls handled by probate and wills staff. The AI assesses over 50 aspects of each call, providing performance scores to managers.

sections.text: A whistleblower called the system "oppressive and dystopian", saying it creates distrust. timeline.text: Covid, Brexit and Liz Truss mini-budget led to lasting decline in mental health, study finds

gist: Major national and global shocks have caused a lasting decline in UK mental health.
The Brexit referendum and the first Covid lockdown caused the most significant psychological distress.
Heightened distress has persisted, leaving NHS mental health services struggling to cope with demand.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A study found that five major shocks since 2016, including Brexit and the first Covid lockdown, caused a lasting decline in UK mental health. Other shocks included the Ukraine invasion, the second lockdown, and Liz Truss's mini-budget.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The research shows that major government decisions and global events seriously damage mental wellbeing. The resulting psychological distress has persisted, contributing to record numbers of people being too sick to work and NHS services struggling to cope with a near-doubling of patients since 2016.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Professor Peter Fonagy is preparing to publish a government-commissioned inquiry report on Friday exploring the rise in mental illness, ADHD, and autism diagnoses.

fivew: Researchers led by Dr Annie Jeffery of University College London.

gist: Rail regulator rejected plans for new train services on the West Coast Main Line.
Proposals by WSMR, Lumo, and Avanti West Coast were denied due to capacity pressures.
Regulator warned additional trains would reduce timetable resilience and increase passenger delays.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Office of Rail and Road rejected plans for new train services linking London with Wrexham, Rochdale, and Blackpool. Applications from Wrexham, Shropshire and Midlands Railway, Lumo, and Avanti West Coast were denied because the line is under significant pressure.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The regulator concluded that adding more services would remove essential gaps in the timetable needed for trains to recover from disruption, risking worse reliability for all passengers.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Campaigners and operators expressed disappointment with the decision, though local representatives stated they would continue fighting for improved rail connectivity.

fivew: The Office of Rail and Road alongside rail operators including WSMR, Lumo, and Avanti West Coast.

gist: Instinct achieved a ten-billion-dollar valuation despite competition from Meta and OpenAI.
Zach Yadegari raised ten million dollars to launch the AI assistant startup Persona.
Both startups employ text-messaging interfaces to execute everyday digital chores.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Instinct launched an invite-only artificial intelligence agent operating via text messages, reaching a valuation of ten billion dollars in late September whilst competing against Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots. Separately, nineteen-year-old Cal AI co-founder Zach Yadegari raised ten million dollars in a round led by Vine Ventures to launch Persona, another personal assistant startup.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Both companies are designing consumer-oriented assistants to manage everyday tasks like bookings and shopping. While Instinct relies on messaging platforms, Persona combines its agent with a wearable band. Industry analysts suggest that although some agents are presently free, future business models will probably depend on advertising or subscription fees.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Persona plans to release its wearable device in December alongside an application. Meanwhile, Instinct intends to keep its service affordable, though analysts note that venture-backed agents may increasingly integrate sponsored recommendations.

fivew: Instinct founder Noah Shinn and Persona co-founder Zach Yadegari.
Startups are releasing conversational AI agents designed to automate everyday consumer chores.
Instinct launched in August, whilst Persona raised funding ahead of a December launch.
San Francisco is the host city for TechCrunch Disrupt, where Yadegari is speaking.
Founders aim to integrate assistants into daily life to turn conversation into action.

sections.text: Startup Goodfire released a monitoring system for AI agents that observes internal model signals. gist: OpenAI told investors its revenue projection is lower than recently indicated.

US tech stocks fell following the news of the revenue gap.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: OpenAI informed investors that its projected revenue is significantly lower than a figure shared previously. While earlier reports suggested an annualized revenue approaching a much higher amount, the company clarified that the actual figure is about fifty billion dollars. The difference occurred because investors tried to compare the figures directly with a rival firm that includes cloud partner sales, whereas OpenAI excludes them.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Market observers closely monitor artificial intelligence revenue forecasts as signs of overall sector demand. The revelation affected technology shares, causing the Nasdaq and several major chip and software companies to decline as markets digested the update.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: OpenAI is reportedly holding early talks for a massive funding round and has delayed its expected stock market float. Meanwhile, rival firms are pressing ahead with their own plans, and investment leaders continue efforts to raise substantial funds for artificial intelligence ventures.

fivew: OpenAI revealed its projected revenue is twenty billion dollars lower than recently indicated to investors.

gist: The US government has blocked Microsoft and other tech firms from a foreign worker program.
Vice President JD Vance accused Microsoft of abusing visas to replace American workers.
Microsoft denied the claims, stating most applications were for existing, well-paid staff.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The US government has suspended Microsoft and seven other technology firms, including Adobe, from a program that helps foreign workers obtain permanent US residency. Vice President JD Vance accused the companies of abusing the H-1B visa system to replace American workers with cheaper foreign labour. The Department of Labor announced it will not process new or pending applications from these firms.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Vance claimed Microsoft laid off American workers while filing thousands of visa applications, undercutting domestic wages. Microsoft rejected these allegations, stating that eighty per cent of its H-1B filings were for existing employees rather than new hires, and that its international staff receive the same compensation as US workers. Immigration advocacy groups argue that attracting global talent benefits the US economy, while Vance described the visa recipients as "indentured servants".

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Microsoft plans to provide the US administration with additional information regarding its hiring practices. Meanwhile, the US government has proposed eliminating the sixty-day grace period for laid-off visa holders.

quotes.text: No company in the US has abused this system more than Microsoft,
the vast majority of Microsoft employees in the United States are Americans.

timeline.text: Let's Encrypt cuts certificate lifetimes to 64 days starting February 2027

gist: Let's Encrypt will shorten free certificate lifetimes to 64 days in February 2027.
Testing for the 64-day certificates begins on October 14.
A 45-day default lifespan is planned to follow in 2028.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Let's Encrypt announced it will reduce free certificate lifespans from 90 days down to 64 days, beginning February 10, 2027. Testing for these shorter certificates is scheduled to start on October 14, allowing users to opt in and check their configurations. Furthermore, lifespans are expected to decrease further to 45 days in 2028.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The change aims to encourage administrators to adopt full ACME automation and use ACME Renewal Information rather than relying on manual processes or hardcoded renewal schedules. Shorter validity periods help limit potential damage and vulnerabilities if private keys are stolen or if certificates are misassigned.

fivew: Let's Encrypt is reducing free SSL/TLS certificate lifetimes to 64 days.

timeline.text: Running out of royals: why calls are growing to let Japan’s princess Aiko take the throne

gist: Calls are growing in Japan to allow Princess Aiko to take the throne.
A 140-year-old law forbids women from ascending to the Chrysanthemum throne.
Conservative government changes safeguard male-only succession despite strong public support for change.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Princess Aiko is the popular only child of Emperor Naruhito and Empress Masako. Under a long-standing law, women cannot ascend to the throne. Recent amendments backed by the government of Sanae Takaichi safeguard male-only succession by allowing women to retain royal status after marriage and resurrecting male-line descendants from collateral branches.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The imperial family is shrinking, leaving very few male heirs in the line of succession. Opinion polls show strong public support for a female emperor to avert a looming succession crisis, but conservative leaders insist on maintaining the male-line tradition.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Amendments safeguarding male-only succession go into effect later this month, but public unease and Aiko's popularity may continue to fuel the debate over female emperors.

fivew: Princess Aiko, Emperor Naruhito, and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.
A looming succession crisis driven by a shrinking royal family clashes with public support for a female emperor.

quotes.text: The unparalleled historic fact that the imperial line has been maintained through the male line for 126 generations is the foundation of the emperor’s authority and legitimacy.

It is important for society to keep progressing ... I believe the duty of the imperial family is to act in response to the requests of society ... I do not think there are any differences between women and men.

sections.text: A masked gang of at least seven people stole 30,000 bottles of prestigious wine, worth €5m, from the Marchesi Antinori winery in Tuscany. She rushed off air and was hospitalised, but had suffered a panic attack.
Hammond returned to the show a week later to discuss her experience.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: During a live broadcast of ITV's This Morning last Friday, presenter Alison Hammond rushed off air after experiencing what she feared was a heart attack. She was taken to hospital, where tests revealed she had actually suffered a panic attack. Hammond described the experience as "very real" and one of the scariest things she had ever been through.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The incident highlighted the intense pressure of presenting live television. Returning to the show a week later, Hammond and psychologist Dr Sian Williams discussed panic attacks to raise awareness. Williams explained that panic attacks represent "anxiety on overdrive" and can feel identical to heart attacks due to shared physical symptoms like chest pain.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Hammond has returned to her regular presenting slot on This Morning. She noted that the health scare has given her a new perspective, prompting her to take stock of her health.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor surrendered his lease on Royal Lodge, incurring dilapidation and repair charges. Deducting £302,000 in early departure compensation left £1.5m owed to the landlord. The King covered this settlement using private funds, though The Times reported that he contributed to the repair costs.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The King intervened to ensure the Crown Estate was not left out of pocket. Mountbatten-Windsor had previously relocated to Sandringham amid controversy surrounding his ties to Jeffrey Epstein. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: At Abric Romaní in Spain, mineral-rich water coated wooden Neanderthal tools in limestone crust. As the wood rotted, it left hollow molds. Spanish archaeologists cataloged 597 wooden remains dating from 62,000 to 40,000 years ago, including thirteen modified tools like spears, bark trays, and a club.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Because wood rots quickly, very little is known about Paleolithic woodwork. These finds show that woodworking was routine for Neanderthals, demonstrating planning and cognitive complexity that challenge the perception of Neanderthals as simple.

gist: An infected Kenyan businessman travelled across three countries before dying from Ebola in Nairobi.
His infection went undetected through several medical facilities and two airport health screenings.
Dozens of potential contacts have been quarantined as health authorities trace his movements.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A Kenyan businessman fell ill in DR Congo, visited several medical facilities, and crossed into Uganda. He then flew to Nairobi via Entebbe, passing airport temperature screenings undetected. Diagnosed with Ebola after arriving at Nairobi Hospital, he died on 5 October.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The incident exposed weaknesses in regional biosecurity and airport screening during an outbreak that has killed over 4,000 people in DR Congo. Experts warned that relying solely on temperature checks is limited, as medications or absence of fever can mask symptoms.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: In September 2022, underwater explosions ruptured the Nord Stream pipelines beneath the Baltic Sea. Following an investigation, German police traced evidence to Ukraine and arrested former Special Forces soldier Serhii K in Italy. Prosecutors allege he led deep-sea divers on a rented yacht to plant explosives. Both Serhii K and Ukraine deny involvement.

sections.text: The blasts severed Russian gas deliveries to Germany, raising questions over attacks on civilian infrastructure. The trial causes diplomatic unease between Berlin and Kyiv. sections.heading: What happens next

He regrets carrying undiagnosed childhood trauma for decades before seeking help at age 60.
Rex now focuses on enjoying ordinary moments and preparing for the end of his life.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Rex Mackrill, aged 65, was diagnosed with incurable stage four prostate cancer after monitoring his family-linked PSA levels. He underwent chemotherapy and hormone treatment, which forced him to stop working as a GP practice manager. Decades earlier, at age 60, he was diagnosed with PTSD following childhood trauma.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Rex's experience highlights the impact of delayed PTSD diagnoses and the benefits of therapies like CBT and EMDR. His terminal diagnosis changed his perspective, teaching him to find joy in ordinary moments and encouraging others to seek support early and discuss end-of-life plans.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Rex is spending his remaining time writing poetry, donating his possessions, and participating in end-of-life planning sessions at Longfield Hospice to ease the burden on his family.

fivew: A man living with terminal cancer reflects on his life, childhood trauma, and finding joy in the present.

gist: Four Conservative candidates have declared their run for the London mayoral nomination.
The Conservative Party has only won the London mayoralty once in 26 years.
The final shortlist of two candidates is expected to be announced in November.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Four Conservative candidates have declared their bids to run for London mayor in the May 2028 election. The declared runners are Sir James Cleverly, Festus Akinbusoye, Andrew Boff, and Alex Challoner.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The Conservatives have only won the London mayoralty once in 26 years, with Boris Johnson. Since then, they have lost three consecutive elections to Labour's Sadiq Khan. However, the party hopes to regain ground following local election victories in Westminster and Wandsworth in May 2026.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The hopefuls must wait until November to see if they make the final shortlist. London party members are expected to choose between the final two candidates, who will likely be announced on 20 November.

gist: Family calls for allergy ratings after a girl died from an unwashed blender.
A cafe and its proprietor were fined following a fatal allergic reaction.
Food safety officials emphasise that businesses must take allergen risks seriously.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A 12-year-old girl died of anaphylactic shock after drinking a milkshake from a south-east London cafe. The blender used had not been washed after making a previous drink containing tree nuts. The cafe and its proprietor were subsequently fined after admitting charges related to food safety.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The family argue that current food hygiene ratings do not inform consumers about a business's allergy management systems. They are campaigning for a dedicated allergy rating scheme so people with food allergies can make safer choices.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Food Standards Agency states it is keeping its policy under review and has produced new guidance and training for businesses regarding allergen responsibilities.

gist: A man released under the early release scheme was jailed days later for shoplifting.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Michael Bogle was released from HMP Wandsworth on 1 October under the government's early release scheme. Within four days, he stole more than £100 worth of detergent from north London supermarkets. gist: England secured a valuable 3-1 first-leg win over Greece in World Cup qualifying.
Maya le Tissier scored her first international goal while making her 15th cap.
Sarina Wiegman debuted teenager Erica Meg Parkinson and handed a debut to Grace Fisk.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: England won 3-1 against Greece in Crete on Friday night during their Women's World Cup qualifying play-off first leg. Maya le Tissier scored in the 63rd minute, while Sarina Wiegman handed debuts to Erica Meg Parkinson and Grace Fisk.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The victory gives England a first-leg lead as they attempt to secure their place in Brazil next year. However, defensive lapses and a failure to keep a clean sheet left Wiegman admitting frustrations over the team's sloppiness.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: England will face Greece again in the second leg on Tuesday in Leicester to finish the job, with the winner advancing to face Ukraine or Slovakia in round two.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Authorities in Portugal suspended the decision to end Rui Pinto's witness protection programme after the Ministry of Justice stated the commission failed to adequately notify him or give him a chance to challenge the ruling. Pinto was given 10 days to assess a risk assessment.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Pinto is the Portuguese computer hacker who founded Football Leaks and released confidential documents that helped trigger the Premier League investigation into Manchester City, who were recently found guilty of breaching financial regulations.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Pinto will assess the risk assessment provided by the special security programmes commission within 10 days.

timeline.text: Time to rise? Ranking European football's sleeping giants

gist: European football features several historic clubs currently playing outside their top domestic divisions.
Criteria for inclusion involve history, heritage, fanbase, stadium capacity, and previous success.
Many of these sleeping giants have experienced financial trouble and recent ownership changes.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Several once-mighty European football clubs, such as Bursaspor, Bordeaux, and Sampdoria, have experienced severe financial difficulties, relegations, and ownership changes in recent years, leaving them competing outside their domestic top flights.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: These clubs boast rich histories, large fanbases, and significant stadium capacities. Their current struggles highlight the fragile nature of football heritage amidst financial instability.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Many of these fallen giants are under new ownership, undergoing stadium redevelopments, and attempting to climb back up their domestic football pyramids.

Why is JJ Gabriel in Man Utd's team photo?

gist: JJ Gabriel features in Manchester United's official team photo despite efforts to leave.
Europe's top clubs are interested in the teenager as he holds a European Union passport.
His decision to seek a move was triggered by non-inclusion against Sabah FK.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: JJ Gabriel is included in Manchester United's official team photo for the season. The pictures were taken before he informed the club of his intention to leave. His exit decision was triggered by not being included in the squad to face Sabah FK.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Gabriel is a target for several top European clubs, including Real Madrid and Barcelona. Manchester United hold his registration and would consider legal action if illegal inducement emerges.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Gabriel is set to turn 16 and his next involvement in a United game will virtually certainly be as an opposition player.
